transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is actually normal for plastic tubs to remain damp after a cycle because they cool down quickly and don't hold enough heat to evaporate water. Rinse aid helps water sheet off dishes rather than bead up; please check if the reservoir is full. Additionally, Eco programmes often skip the heated drying phase to save energy, so plastics will stay wet on those settings.
The rinse aid reservoir is empty, the symbol is lit. I use all-in-one tablets though. I always run Eco 50 and open the door straight away at the end. Does that matter?

Opening the door straight away does matter: it lets steam escape before the dishes cool down, which can actually help them dry rather than stay wet from condensation. However, the main issue is likely that you are using all-in-one tablets with an empty rinse aid reservoir. All-in-one tablets contain a small amount of rinse aid, but not enough for good drying; without topping up the separate rinse aid dispenser, water beads on dishes instead of sheeting off. Please top up the rinse aid and try a standard cycle next time to see if that resolves it.
ok, I'll fill the rinse aid up and see. Do you think I should stop using Eco 50 too, or is the rinse aid enough?

Topping up the rinse aid is essential because it helps water sheet off dishes rather than bead up; without it, even a standard cycle will leave plastics wet. However, Eco 50 is designed to save energy by using lower temperatures and often skips or reduces the heated drying phase, so plastics will likely remain damp on that setting regardless of rinse aid levels. For best results with all-in-one tablets (which have limited rinse aid content), switch to a standard cycle like 'Auto' or 'Normal' which typically includes a more effective drying phase. If you continue using Eco 50, keep opening the door at the end as you are doing, but expect plastics to stay wet.
